ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the positive feedback loop of oxytocin during childbirth. The fetal head presses on the cervix, the cervix produces nerve impulses and transmits them to the brain; the brain stimulates the pituitary gland to secrete oxytocin; oxytocin is transported through the blood to the uterus; oxytocin promotes uterine contractions, pushing the fetus further toward the cervix; the fetal head then presses more strongly on the cervix, causing this cycle to continue to strengthen. Reasoning: The common pattern reflected in this diagram is: an initial stimulus triggers a response, and the response product then strengthens the original stimulus or activates more similar responses. Applying this pattern to the platelet response when tissue is injured: the injured tissue first releases chemical signals to activate nearby platelets; the activated platelets also release chemical substances; these substances further activate more platelets; more activated platelets continue to release signals, causing platelet aggregation and the coagulation response to be continuously amplified, forming positive feedback.
